ns1:item.ns1:title: The Palæo Data Cube: A Digital Earth of the past inspired by present-day Big Earth Observations Data practices
ns1:item.dc:title: The Palæo Data Cube: A Digital Earth of the past inspired by present-day Big Earth Observations Data practices
ns1:item.dc:creator: Florian Franziskakis Christian Vérard Jean-Philippe Richard Sébastien Castelltort Gregory Giuliani a Institute for Environmental Sciences, enviroSPACE Lab, University of Geneva, Geneva, Switzerlandb Department of Earth Sciences, Earth Surface Dynamics Group, University of Geneva, Geneva, Switzerlandc Institute for Environmental Sciences, University of Geneva, Geneva, SwitzerlandA close-up portrait photograph of a man in a suit jacket and collared shirt, facing forward.A close-up portrait photograph of a man in a suit jacket and collared shirt, facing forward.Florian Franziskakis is a Lecturer and PhD Candidate at the Institute for Environmental Sciences, University of Geneva. His work focuses on applying geographic information system (GIS) tools for Earth science modelling, particularly reconstructing the Earth’s evolution in deep-time. Previously, he worked at the Group on Earth Observations (GEO) Secretariat where he served as in situ data management specialist, and was also involved in the development of the GEO Knowledge Hub, an open digital library for Earth observation applications.A man with a beard smiling at the camera.A man with a beard smiling at the camera.Christian Vérard is a Senior Researcher at the Department of Earth Sciences, University of Geneva (UNIGE). His research focuses on global plate tectonic modelling, with particular expertise in deep-time paleogeographic reconstructions and their implications for long-term climate change. He developed PANALESIS, a plate tectonic model covering Earth’s entire surface from the Neoproterozoic to the present.A man smiling, wearing a blue shirt, with a blurred green background.A man smiling, wearing a blue shirt, with a blurred green background.Jean-Philippe Richard joined GRID-Geneva in 1999, initially focusing on the development of metadata database projects. Since 2010, he has served as the IT Officer for GRID-Geneva, overseeing server management and core infrastructure. In addition to his role as system administrator, he actively participates in the development of web, database, and GIS projects. He is one of the primary developers for the Ramsar Convention’s RSIS platform and a core member of the Swiss Data Cube technical team.A man in a suit and tie, facing the camera.A man in a suit and tie, facing the camera.Sébastien Castelltort is a Full Professor of Earth Sciences at the University of Geneva. His research focuses on source-to-sink dynamics, investigating how climate, tectonics, and surface processes control sediment production, transport, and deposition in modern and ancient systems. He has conducted field and modeling studies worldwide and has worked extensively on past global warming events, including the Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum.Gregory Giuliani serves as Head of the Digital Earth Unit and Project Leader of the Swiss Data Cube at GRID-Geneva, United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), and holds the position of Senior Lecturer at the University of Geneva’s Institute for Environmental Sciences. He is a geologist and environmental scientist who specializes in Remote Sensing, Geographical Information Systems (GIS) and Spatial Data Infrastructures (SDI). He also works at GRID-Geneva of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) since 2001, where he was previously the focal point for Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI). Dr. Giuliani’s research focuses on Land Change Science and how Earth observations can be used to monitor and assess environmental changes and support sustainable development initiatives.Photograph of a man smiling in a close-up portrait, wearing a collared shirt.Photograph of a man smiling in a close-up portrait, wearing a collared shirt.
